steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Long have you walked the land, Kal'tsit. The changes in the sky would not have escaped your attention.
The Seaborn raises its head slightly, gazing up with its non-existent eyes. Perhaps a habit from the time it still had them.
Above the dome, beyond the infinite water, something in the distance seems to have caught its attention.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Tell me, how long will it take for the hole to close again?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...I see.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Ægir was right. The Seaborn had a clear reason for leaving the ocean and invading the land.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You came because you noticed the change in the barrier.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: I have seen through the eyes of we many who have ventured on land.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: There is a ripple in the sky. The immutable veil has been torn open.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your survival instincts have driven you to monitor every change in the environment... and the dangers they signify.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Dangers? Yes.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: You are indeed sharp, Kal'tsit. Your program runs smoothly.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Our communication will be, effective.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: The calamity that hangs above Terra. The eye that gazes upon us. Does it see the abnormality of the sky? Or has it already...

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: You understand Terra, Kal'tsit, and the crisis it faces.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: You can. You must. Help we many understand, help we many evolve.

options: Am I hearing this correctly, Kal'tsit?
Rhodes Island came to eliminate you.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: I sincerely hope this is the Seaborn's wishful thinking, rather than some kind of consensus you have, Dr. Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Let it finish, Madame Consul.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: The last chance is fleeting. The oceans of Terra are too small.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Knowledge. Nourishment. Space. We many must grow. We many require help.

options: You're not just trying to go on land?
You want to go into space?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Growing wings is not difficult, but insufficient. Going beyond the skies requires a revolution in the species' fundamental nature.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: You have the knowledge, Kal'tsit. You help we many understand, and we overcome calamity.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Whatever their origin, the Seaborn are non-sapient creatures driven by instinct, ones that the Church fanatics have placed their unreasonable expectations on.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But you know far more than either of those two groups possibly could. How?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: We are the same, Kal'tsit. You and we many, have the same duty.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Perhaps I should reframe the question...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: How did the Seaborn evolve into what they are today? What do you have to do with Caerula Arbor going out of control?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Is the answer important to you?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: I can speak of my own history, if it helps you understand my intention.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: ...We've waited two centuries for these answers.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: What really happened in that failed expedition? What turned you into what you are now?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Failed? No. It was a success beyond our wildest dreams.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: We penetrated the deepest layer of the mantle ruins for the first time.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: The Predecessors carved open the rock and built massive, maze-like complexes reaching into the lower mantle. We'd never gone further than them, even after thousands of years of excavating.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: The mantle ruins, the genesis of Ægir civilization. We thought we'd find more relics, more secrets, more answers there.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: But all we had hoped for did not exist. All that was buried in those depths was a spark of hope.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Go on.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: I was separated from my team along the way. I was the only one to make it to the end of the path.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: There, I saw...

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: A giant. Some massive thing sleeping in the shadow of the cerulean tree.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: I did not see His entirety. A small part of His limb was enough to fill my entire vision.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: That limb was touching the transparent wall of a sealed chamber. Perhaps He was waiting for contact, or perhaps...

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Before I realized it, I was standing before Him and reaching out.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: The wall of the chamber was cold, but I could feel His warmth. Then, visions surged towards me from every direction, inundating me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: A Feranmut shared its vision with you. What did you see?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Fallen cities under an oppressively hanging dome, the land aflame, the stargate extinguished, the Star Ring broken, the road network shattered...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The destruction of prehistoric civilization?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Yes. Ægir never discovered the reason for its destruction, but I saw a vision of it before my eyes.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Yet it was not the end. Visions continued to flow, visions far beyond my limited comprehension.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Eternally dispersing particles and oceans of sand that never ripple...

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Cold, lightless plains and darkness without end...

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Burnt-out stars and ever-expanding black holes...

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Nothing there was familiar. I lost my senses, all of them, and even the Feranmut that shared vision with me could not sense His own existence...

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: It was an entirely alien place, without life, meaning, or information—
The Seaborn's words stop. Through its transparent skull, you can see the strangely colored nuclei gather, then disperse.
It seems to be thinking, and the nuclei represent the process of its thoughts.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: But you, Kal'tsit, understand the meaning of those images.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...The crisis destroyed everything. It cannot be visualized; there is no word in our language to describe it.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: It was the end of prehistoric civilization, and the calamity that Terra must face. It is the end of all things.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: The horrifying images left me as I pulled my hand back, replaced by another image. One that was broken, blurred, chaotic.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: He and His children shall devour all that is living, and consume the moons and the stars. All that is living and dead shall nourish Him, and He shall murmur at the end of time—

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: 'Survive.'

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Over and over. Survive.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: 'Chaotic', 'murmur'... was the Feranmut asleep?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: He was trapped within a dream. The dream stagnated, evolution stagnated, duty stagnated. He was trapped in the cerulean cave.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Therefore, I must awaken Him.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Cassia!

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: Magister Avitus.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Did you and your comrades go into hiding in order to destroy the city from within? Waiting for when the Sea Patrol's guard was at its weakest?

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: You should be evacuating, Magister.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: The Sea Patrol has noticed, Cassia. They're investigating you.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: You're showing this much concern for me because that tiny embryo I left in the incubator reminded you of the past, am I right?

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: I'm just curious: Do you regret your decision?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Now is not the time for this.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: The Seaborn have invaded Milliarium. Stop what you're doing, or the city will be lost.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: Isn't it a little late for that?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Why did you...

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: Choose to betray Ægir?

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: I told you. The Seaborn have revealed the weakness of Ægir's very foundation. Before people can regain the will to live, the collapse of their values will have crushed them already.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: Once, you were a great scholar. But what are you doing in this city now?

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: You found out about me a long time ago, didn't you? You had many chances to stop things from getting to this point. You could have reported me to the Sea Patrol at any time.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: But you did nothing. You sat and waited, watching everything happen like a blind fin spinning in a whirlpool.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: Did you come to Milliarium just to witness the destruction, and validate your own despair?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: I'm not... I can still stop you.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: As long as life remains tied to any value system, it is doomed to eventually collapse. Life itself should be reason enough to live.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: We must rekindle our most basic survival instincts, and force the people to reassess the values they once held in such high regard.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: Only by doing so can they be saved from despair. From becoming like you.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Like me...
Watch out!

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: (Cries and buzzes excitedly)

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Hmph... Cassia got away.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: The linkage here was sabotaged. No wonder it didn't work from the control room!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: L-Leave this to me, ma'am.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: The Seaborn are approaching.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: My mentor at the Inquisition taught me some Arts... although my talents are nothing to write home about.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: That woman worked at the Institute of Facility Management. She'd know how to sabotage the city unit framework...

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I appreciate your courage, Jordi. I'll call in people to get this area under control. As for Cassia, she's mine.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: (Rapidly flaps fins)

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Wh-Whoa! Already?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Are you going to keep lying there, Mr. Avitus?
His student had vanished. Avitus gazes upon the young man who suddenly appeared before him. The fear in Jordi's eyes is obvious, but he lights his lantern with a trembling hand.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Jordi...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I heard your conversation.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: You... You're not an evil man. But I'm disappointed in you. Very disappointed.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Did you come here with this city because you believed it wouldn't make it back?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: What are you hoping for? Death?

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: You should have returned to land sooner, Jordi.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Look around us. The Seaborn will soon overcome the barrier between the city's units. It will all come to an end, just like—

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: You never answer my questions properly!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I may end up leaving Ægir, and leaving behind all my hopes and longings, but it won't be because it's about to be destroyed.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I've read 'The Death of Life,' you know, but it didn't answer any of my questions.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Let's say all your predictions come true, and that at some point in the future we'll have no choice but to watch our homes come to the end it depicts, just like that man in the book.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But does the destruction of a civilization really weigh more than that of a city, a family, or a person, here and now?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I don't understand. I just... don't.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I wasn't sure if I should say this, but...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: You said your Familiar gave up on the idea of raising a child and died in disappointment. But was she disappointed in the future of Ægir, or...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: In you?
The young Ægir musters all his strength. The lantern shakes violently, and the flickering light repels the Seaborn.
He gasps for air. Sweat rolls down his cheeks. Avitus can see his arm tremble, but if anything, it is himself who cuts a sorrier figure.

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: ...Look out!

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You have smeared your bodies on the outer wall, infiltrating through the trail of weapon fire before reshaping. What a convenient form of life.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Seaborn.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: (Joyfully convulses its gelatinous body)

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: (Excitedly sways fine tentacles)

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: You, here.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Nest, we, seen. From nest, you, leave. Incomprehension.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Ul-pianus, kin. You, here, wait, us.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Ul-pianus. Ul-pianus. No, confusion?

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: (Pained convulsions)

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: No, need, pain.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Individual death, eternal. The many's survival, eternal.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Ul-pianus, I, lead, you. New individual, born, for you, help you... extend me...

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Gladiia.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: *Cough*—Ulpianus.
There is no expression on Gladiia's face. She holds her lance sideways, its point touching the floor.
An almost imperceptible posture, enough to mitigate the fatigue that continues to rush up from within her, and to support her as she stands before her long-absent colleague.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Your 'friend' is now a pool of goo, but you still need to answer its question.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Such rowdiness. This is really poor dance etiquette, you know?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Ha—

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Dance is an art. It's all about elegance. You can't make it work with strength of numbers.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: What? That didn't pierce it.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: This used to be a cluster of coral changed by the Seaborn, but now it's a wall. No one knows how thick it is.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The warning from the city, the unusual movements of the Seaborn, the results of the abnormal surgery... We must get out of here and find out what's happening at Milliarium.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: The entrance is gone?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: No, it's us. We're losing our sense of direction.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Capsidization... Everything around us is hardening. The algal blanket, the unhatched eggs, even the waves.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: This entire nest will become a hardened shell for these creatures to store their nutrients. A shell without a single crack. There is no way the three of us can...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Even worse, the stagnating environment is exacerbating our exhaustion.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Captain Gladiia? Shark?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Behind you—

steps.name: Gentle Seaborn
steps.text: (Hums gently)

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Eww.

steps.name: Gentle Seaborn
steps.text: Nest, become whole. Soon, the sea.

steps.name: Gentle Seaborn
steps.text: You, kin. No harm.

steps.name: Gentle Seaborn
steps.text: We many accept you. We many protect you.

steps.name: Gentle Seaborn
steps.text: Here, much nutrient. Sleep. Only sleep.
The lethargy, which had heretofore been suppressed by the fighting, begins to spread through every limb and organ.
The thick and hard shell solidifies the waves. All is stagnant. The Hunters vaguely sense their consciousness sinking, as though there is no bottom. The Hunters hear the song—
Coming from right beside them, coming from inside them—
'Ishar-mla.'
'The hardship we suffer is ever present.'
'The life we thirst for is ever present.'

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Over there... Skadi...
Roaring.
The faint roar comes from above. The thundering roar comes from beside. The stagnant seawater flows again.
The infinite ocean could be bound by a cocoon. Then, from where comes the force that can break even the cocoon?
Land. Moon. The scent of wheat. Home far away.
The force has become legend. It has shattered mountains, death, time, all that is tangible and intangible—
He will not be bound.

steps.name: Rocinante
steps.text: (Loud neigh)

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: You, many, alike...

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: From where...

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Hraaagh—

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: The waves, you built them, you hardened them.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Are you... turning this to land?

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Will not allow.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Contradiction. Wilderness, mountains, rivers, wheat fields. Land is just land.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: I seek, I reproach, I crush.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The one who was with Ulpianus...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Whew... A pleasure to see you again, Sir Knight.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: You, not kin.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: (Furious roar)—!

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: (Agitatedly twitches soft tentacles)

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: (Excitedly flaps creased fins)

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Out of the way!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Doña Irene!

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I've been looking for you.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Sorry, I...

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Received Consul Clementia's message? Dr. Kal'tsit's group is headed to the port, but then we lost communications again.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: We must return to the Eye of Iberia immediately, inform Lord Carmen, and help the Inquisition and Penal Battalion form defense lines.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: No. We have to wait.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Most of the invading Seaborn are still under control near the beacon tower. If that unit can be ejected...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Then Milliarium is not yet lost. It can even organize a counterattack.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But the cultists have sabotaged the linkage to prevent it from being jettisoned.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: The Sea Patrol is already cleaning up the Seaborn in the area. We can't let these slip away either.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I'll deal with them. As for whatever this linkage is you're talking about... Will your engineering skills help?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Yes!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I can fix it!

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Good. You take the lead on that.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I'll protect you and Avitus. We can return to land as soon as we're done.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: We worked together at the Eye of Iberia. Let's pray we do just as well this time.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: But these Seaborn from the depths are different from the ones I've dealt with on land. I don't know how long I can hold them off.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: We've said all that needs to be said, Mr. Avitus. Come and help, if you still have the strength!

steps.name: Avitus
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Hurry, Jordi!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Hurry, Jordi Fontanarossa!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You warned us through the beacon... And the strange knight who appeared at the lighthouse broke through the shell just as we were about to fall asleep.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Is he part of your plan too, Ulpianus?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The madman who's forgotten himself is an enemy of the sea, of everything abnormal that has become normal, and of himself.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: No one can control someone like that. We just happened to travel together.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Are you the only one to make it back?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: They're on their way.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Breaking through the nest's shell and returning through tides of Seaborn... Your speed was remarkable, but you're too late.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You've seen what's happening to Milliarium. The many have exploited Ægir, and Milliarium will be the stepping stone for their invasion of the land.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: And what, precisely, is happening here?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The first thing I heard when I arrived at the port is that the Abyssal Hunter, Ulpianus, had entered the control room of the beacon tower and killed the weapons technology advisor of the Waterway Program.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: And indeed, Blandus's body is right behind you.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You're quiet.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I assumed you'd feel more anguish over him.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I take it you've figured him out then, judging by your reaction.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I doubt we have time to discuss a fallen traitor... even if he was once our closest comrade.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: That young man really did it.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The linkage has been repaired.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You're trying to eject the beacon tower from Milliarium... A wise plan.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: It seems there's still hope for you.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: This place will sink to the ocean floor in a few minutes. Do you smell it?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The stench of frenzy...The Seaborn above have noticed the changes to the tower. They're seizing the last opportunity to break the blockade and reach the other parts of Milliarium.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Leave, Gladiia. Now.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Come back to Ægir, Ulpianus. This is your last chance.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I still have things to clear up. If I give up now, all my efforts will have been for naught.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The dreams and end of the prehistoric civilization, where the Seaborn came from, where they will go, the calamity before our eyes, the destruction beyond the skies...

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Being aware of them is not enough to turn the tides. I must learn more.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: If the Seaborn have memories, I must know every last detail of them.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I'm not disputing that. We're back in the ocean, back in Ægir. We'll have many chances to approach the truth.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: That is your way. And I don't disapprove. But we need more approaches, more angles, in order to maximize our odds of victory.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: As you've said, I'm on another path now.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Will you still try to stop me?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Unless my eyes deceived me, the Seaborn I just killed had evolved specifically for you.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: That doesn't just mean they are trying to accept you. It means that you also...

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Correct.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Then you know well what being inside a rapidly hatching nest would mean for you, in your present state.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Answer me, Ægir. How much of your mind is still your own?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Is there even enough left for you to choose death?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: It's the only way for me to earn the trust of these scum.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: You're an outstanding Hunter, and a learned scientist. Are you really so arrogant as to believe you can control your transformation through willpower alone?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Accidents like the one during the auto-adaptive junction surgery will not happen every time.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I can't simply watch you walk down the path of destruction.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: ...You're at your limit.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: We're both experts in violence. You'll die if we fought here and now.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Is that so?
Her lance draws a cold arc through the air. Ulpianus lets loose the chains, and his massive anchor flies at Gladiia, forcing her to leap up.
The sound of the building sinking drowns out the clash of metal. Seawater and Seaborn rush into the control room.
In the last moments, Gladiia watches her erstwhile colleague stand before the darkened holographic sea chart, calmly waiting for the colorful waves to swallow him.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your description raises many questions.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The feasibility of modifying a Feranmut into a biological ark by leveraging its habit of fostering an independent ecosystem inside its body had already been verified on Talos.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The technology used by the project was mature.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And their complex was deep in the mantle. Energy coming from the heart of the planet could support the facilities' operation for almost an eternity.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The project had more than sufficient power supply.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Why, then, did the project deep beneath the ocean 'stagnate,' as you put it, and go out of control, releasing innumerable Seaborn?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: The existence of Feranmut was introverted by nature, yet He was to turn all things to nourishment for His survival. He was given meaning that did not belong to Him, and a name that did not belong to Him—Ishar-mla.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: The changes They were put to were bolder, wilder, more ambitious, and more despairing. Their nature had long since exceeded the biological ark you speak of.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: For unknown reasons, however, Their subsequent actions did not follow the program.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Meaning that the project did not proceed along the planned lines, but the new direction was also interrupted?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Not entirely. He—They continue to foster new offspring within themselves.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: But the lives trapped within the Feranmut were weak. They evolved too slowly.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: The new generation needed to be liberated. They needed to leave the Feranmut's body, adapt to new environments, and obtain more nutrition.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: More nutrition to be fed back to the Feranmut, so that His evolution may be accelerated.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Under normal circumstances, the organisms nurtured within a Feranmut are rarely able to venture beyond its body. Yet the aggression the Seaborn have demonstrated outside...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The modifications these Feranmuts have undergone were indeed transformative.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: So it was you, Mártus, who brought the Seaborn into the ocean, and sowed the seeds of calamity.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Seeds of calamity? No, the offspring were weak, and Ægir was strong.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: The seabed was governed by a self-regulating ecosystem. Offspring that devoured the algae fields would be discovered and destroyed before they could proliferate.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: But Ægir should not have been an obstacle. Ægir should have provided aid. Fortunately, my influence in human society was still useful.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The Institute of Development Planning had already announced the deaths of the members of the fourth observation team of the mantle ruins at that time... You 'came back from the dead' just to corrupt your countrymen?!

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: I held no forums, no debates, only a few sincere conversations. I helped some discover the problem, and some discover the answer.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: It was enough that they were willing to give the Seaborn an opportunity. We many will find a way out eventually.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The ecological disasters, the fallen cities, the citizens lost... How many of those were you responsible for?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Was it you who cajoled Blandus and the cultists behind him to infiltrate the Waterway Program and alter our weapon systems?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: (The nuclei within its skull spin)

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: This so-called Church of the Deep is not a formal organization, at least not in the sea.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: It needs no guidance, no leader.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Not an organization... You mean you manipulated the people's thoughts and behaviors only using their faith and tenets?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: How did you implant the ethereal concept of 'god' into them, when such absurd ideas were completely absent in Ægir?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Civilization could never truly purge the idea of primal worship. It awaits at the end of science, ready to be awakened at a moment's notice.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: The Ægir you call 'cultists' do not know the truth. Each of them acts according to their own thoughts and ideals. Each faces their own questions and dilemmas.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: 'Selfishness and altruism.'

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: 'Flaws and perfection.'

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: 'Nature and civilization.'

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: 'Logic and unreason.'

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: 'The differences in strength and the shackles of form.'

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: 'The limitations of ethics and the future of humanity.'

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: 'A manufactured truth and the beautiful cycle...'

options: It was all a scam from the get-go?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: (The nuclei within its skull spin)

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: A scam? No.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Primal worship originates from the survival instinct.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Every thread of thought by every 'cultist' ultimately leads to a single question: How to survive better.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Faith? Tenets? No, only a desire for survival.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: You struggle for survival too, do you not?

options: When you preached survival in Ægir...
Did you ever tell them whose survival you were talking about?

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: The survival of life itself.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Just as the survival of civilization inevitably involves the destruction of many more, the survival of life inevitably involves the end of many.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Many species have gone extinct due to the activity of the offspring, while they gathered nutrition for the Feranmut. I once recorded the number, only to forget it.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: For the moment Ishar-mla awakened, it had become a meaningless, insignificant number.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: The birth cries of the newborn, interwoven with the wailing of the dying...

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Songs brought Silence.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: You knew the consequences of awakening the Firstborn from the very beginning. A disaster for the entire ocean, for countless species. But you show no remorse whatsoever.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: You even gave up on recording the number of sacrifices. Was it because you'd gone numb after taking so many lives?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: But numbness is no excuse for your crimes, Mártus.
The consul steps forward. Her ceremonial sword is elegant, but the light reflecting off it is chilling, cutting off the sightline of the Seaborn gazing towards you.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The Sophontheatrum. You designed the building that inspired so many of our people... myself included.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: But you stand here now, calmly explaining how you pushed Ægir into the abyss.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: I've seen images of you. A gentle, meditative observer who has the habit of constantly pushing his large glasses back up his nose.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Look at you now. Even the richest of thoughts can only be expressed by the simplistic movements of your cells.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: You still have your glasses on your neck. Is it to reminisce about old friends whom you have no right to reminisce, or to mock the dead whom you have no right to mock?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: If you are Mártus the Ægir, then I hereby pass judgment upon the fallen.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: If you are merely Seaborn, then we'll skip the formalities.
The organelles surrounding the Seaborn expand and parry Clementia's attack. The ceremonial sword cuts into the shadow of the coral-shaped terminal.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: Mm—Gurgle.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: You cut off my control of the terminal?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Breathes scorching fire)

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Howls furiously)

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: Emergency transmission. This is the 10th attempt—

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: The Seaborn have taken over the beacon tower. We cannot stop the conversion! But someone has activated the ejection protocol for that unit—good job, whoever you are!

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: Bio-signatures keep soaring in number. The nests are becoming one—

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: Incoming Seaborn tide! Scope is the entire continental shelf! Repeat, incoming Seaborn tide! Scope is the entire continental shelf!

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: Emergency transmission. This is the 11th attempt—

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: This is Consul Clementia. Citizens of Milliarium, heed me!

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Once the city unit containing the beacon tower has been fully ejected, the rest of the city shall break through the Seaborn encirclement and move towards dry land!

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Reactivate the linkage mechanism in the city's framework and perform a structural reorganization. Force fields at full power! We'll stop the Seaborn tide from setting a single tentacle onto land!

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Legions VIII and X, along with the Sea Patrol: send all operational warships out in turn to escort the city!

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: May Ægir and our forefathers be with you.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: You were looking for an opportunity this whole time... consul of Ægir.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: You're tough.

steps.name: 'Seaborn'
steps.text: We... too. Once.

steps.name: Inquisition Clerk
steps.text: Is it Ægir or the Seaborn who are trying to open up a Waterway? The readings are off the charts. The endless Seaborn tide is approaching us at the very moment...

steps.name: Inquisition Clerk
steps.text: This is beyond the lighthouse's computational capacity!

steps.name: Inquisition Clerk
steps.text: Su Santidad?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: I hear you.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Look in front of you.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Those deep colors between the sea and sky are a tide of Seaborn.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: The wind grows quiet... There is no point in trying to estimate their numbers and scope now.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Experience is better than data. I've seen the ocean like this before.

steps.name: Inquisition Clerk
steps.text: Do you mean the... the Profound Silence?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Leave the rest to the Penal Battalion and the Inquisitors.

steps.name: Penal Battalion Soldier
steps.text: R-Report!

steps.name: Penal Battalion Soldier
steps.text: Two divisions are ready for action. Ægirian drone matrices are helping us fine-tune our defenses.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Ægir...

steps.name: Inquisition Clerk
steps.text: Sir... the ocean... Something's rising from it.

steps.name: Inquisition Clerk
steps.text: Is that... an Ægirian city?
Having sailed for thousands of miles, Milliarium rises to the surface of the ocean after casting out its heart.

Every inch of it is being reformed, supported by its framework. An invisible forcefield extends towards the bottom of the sea and the highest reaches of the sky, forming a structure like a great wall.
The structure breaks the surface of the ocean, creating a giant wave a hundred meters tall. However, on the other side of the city, the real tide has arrived—
It is a living wave. Seaborn of various forms have fused with the ocean. The children of the sea are the sea itself; they have even changed the color of the water.
The city from the depths and the roiling tide stretch out at the same time, colliding, embracing, and ripping at each others' throats.
Nature never tires, yet civilization will not stop its footsteps.
All is quiet. No wind dares tell of what it sees, here and now.
